claim: ZDHHC20-mediated S-acylation of the ORAI1 channel at residue Cys143 promotes TCR recruitment and signaling at the IS.
source: Here, we show that ZDHHC20-mediated S-acylation of the ORAI1 channel at residue Cys143 promotes TCR recruitment and signaling at the IS.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Cys143 mutations reduced ORAI1 currents and store-operated Ca2+ entry in HEK-293 cells.
source: Cys143 mutations reduced ORAI1 currents and store-operated Ca2+ entry in HEK-293 cells
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Cys143 mutations nearly abrogated long-lasting Ca2+ elevations, NFATC1 translocation, and IL-2 secretion evoked by TCR engagement in Jurkat T cells.
source: Cys143 mutations reduced ORAI1 currents and store-operated Ca2+ entry in HEK-293 cells and nearly abrogated long-lasting Ca2+ elevations, NFATC1 translocation, and IL-2 secretion evoked by TCR engagement in Jurkat T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The acylation-deficient channel remained in cholesterol-poor domains upon enforced ZDHHC20 expression.
source: The acylation-deficient channel remained in cholesterol-poor domains upon enforced ZDHHC20 expression
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The acylation-deficient channel was recruited less efficiently to the IS along with actin and TCR.
source: The acylation-deficient channel remained in cholesterol-poor domains upon enforced ZDHHC20 expression and was recruited less efficiently to the IS along with actin and TCR.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: S-acylation is a critical regulator of ORAI1 channel trafficking and function at the IS.
source: Our results establish S-acylation as a critical regulator of ORAI1 channel trafficking and function at the IS
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: ORAI1 S-acylation enhances TCR recruitment to the synapse.
source: Our results establish S-acylation as a critical regulator of ORAI1 channel trafficking and function at the IS and reveal that ORAI1 S-acylation enhances TCR recruitment to the synapse.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Following TCR engagement, the Ca2+ depletion of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) causes the ER-bound Ca2+ sensors STIM1-2 to oligomerise and to accumulate in ER-PM junctions.
source: Following TCR engagement, the Ca2+ depletion of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) causes the ER-bound Ca2+ sensors STIM1-2 to oligomerise and to accumulate in ER-PM junctions (Zhang et al., 2005; Liou et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: STIM1-2 trap and gate the Ca2+-release-activated (CRAC) ORAI1 channel at ER-PM junctions.
source: Following TCR engagement, the Ca2+ depletion of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) causes the ER-bound Ca2+ sensors STIM1-2 to oligomerise and to accumulate in ER-PM junctions (Zhang et al., 2005; Liou et al., 2005), where they trap and gate the Ca2+-release-activated (CRAC) ORAI1 channel (Vig et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Ca2+ influx through ORAI1 sustains long-lasting Ca2+ signals that initiate gene expression programs of T cell proliferation and differentiation.
source: The ensuing Ca2+ influx sustains long-lasting Ca2+ signals that initiate gene expression programs of T cell proliferation and differentiation.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of T cell biology.

claim: Proper ORAI1 function is essential for immunity in humans.
source: Proper ORAI1 function is essential for immunity in humans and patients with ORAI1 mutations suffer from severe combined immunodeficiency (Lacruz and Feske, 2015; Feske et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Patients with ORAI1 mutations suffer from severe combined immunodeficiency.
source: Proper ORAI1 function is essential for immunity in humans and patients with ORAI1 mutations suffer from severe combined immunodeficiency (Lacruz and Feske, 2015; Feske et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: STIM1 binding opens the ORAI1 channel pore.
source: Recent studies have revealed the structural rearrangements occurring within ORAI1 as STIM1 binding opens the channel pore (Hou et al., 2018; Hou et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: STIM1 binding increases ORAI1's selectivity for Ca2+.
source: Recent studies have revealed the structural rearrangements occurring within ORAI1 as STIM1 binding opens the channel pore (Hou et al., 2018; Hou et al., 2020) and increases its selectivity for Ca2+ 11, 12, reviewed in Qiu and Lewis, 2019.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Crystal structure from the highly homologous Drosophila Orai1 channel revealed a hexamer of four concentric TM subunits.
source: Crystal structure from the highly homologous Drosophila Orai1 channel revealed a hexamer of four concentric TM subunits, with pore-lining TM1 helixes bearing an acidic selectivity filter followed by hydrophobic and basic regions (Hou et al., 2018; Hou et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The closed structure of ORAI1 is stabilised by multiple interactions between interlocking TM2 and TM3 helixes and peripheral TM4 helixes.
source: The closed structure is stabilised by multiple interactions between interlocking TM2 and TM3 helixes and peripheral TM4 helixes, bent in three crossed helical pairs extending in the cytosol.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about ORAI1.

claim: STIM1 binds to the external M4 helix of ORAI1, generating a gating signal transmitted by the TM2/TM3 ring to TM1, opening the channel pore and increasing its Ca2+ selectivity.
source: STIM1 binds to the external M4 helix, generating a gating signal transmitted by the TM2/TM3 ring to TM1, opening the channel pore and increasing its Ca2+ selectivity (Zhang et al., 2005; Liou et al., 2005; McNally et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The reversible switch of ORAI1 between a quiescent to an active state is highly regulated to avoid inappropriate Ca2+ fluxes at the wrong time or place.
source: The reversible switch of ORAI1 between a quiescent to an active state is highly regulated to avoid inappropriate Ca2+ fluxes at the wrong time or place (reviewed in Qiu and Lewis, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Protein S-acylation dynamically controls the trafficking and gating of more than 50 ion channels by increasing the hydrophobicity of protein domains.
source: Protein S-acylation, the reversible thioester linkage of a medium length fatty acid, often palmitic acid, on intracellular cysteine residues, dynamically controls the trafficking and gating of more than 50 ion channels by increasing the hydrophobicity of protein domains Shipston, 2011.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: S-acylation regulates ligand-gated (AMPA, GABA, Kainate, nAChR, NMDA, KATP, P2 × 7 receptors), voltage-gated (CaV, KV, KCa NaV), epithelial (ENaC), and water channels (AQP4).
source: S-acylation regulates ligand-gated (AMPA, GABA, Kainate, nAChR, NMDA, KATP, P2 × 7 receptors), voltage-gated (CaV, KV, KCa NaV), epithelial (ENaC), and water channels (AQP4).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of ion channel regulation.

claim: The S-acylation reaction is mediated by zinc-finger and DHHC-domain containing Protein AcylTransferases (PATs) at the ER and Golgi.
source: The S-acylation reaction is mediated by zinc-finger and DHHC-domain containing Protein AcylTransferases (PATs) at the ER and Golgi Ohno et al., 2006
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: S-acylation is reversed by acyl protein thioesterases at the PM.
source: The S-acylation reaction is mediated by zinc-finger and DHHC-domain containing Protein AcylTransferases (PATs) at the ER and Golgi Ohno et al., 2006 and reversed by acyl protein thioesterases at the PM Yokoi et al., 2016
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: 23 PATs and five thioesterases isoforms have been identified in human so far.
source: The S-acylation reaction is mediated by zinc-finger and DHHC-domain containing Protein AcylTransferases (PATs) at the ER and Golgi Ohno et al., 2006 and reversed by acyl protein thioesterases at the PM Yokoi et al., 2016, with 23 PATs and five thioesterases isoforms identified in human so far Tabaczar et al., 2017.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Protein S-acylation impacts the distribution of proteins in membrane microdomains and between intracellular membranes.
source: Due to the hydrophobic nature of the attached acyl moieties, protein S-acylation impacts the distribution of proteins in membrane microdomains and between intracellular membranes Rocks et al., 2010.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The human isoform ORAI1 was identified by acyl-biotinyl exchange chemistry coupled to mass spectrometry as a robustly S-acylated protein in primary human T cells.
source: First, the human isoform ORAI1 was identified by acyl-biotinyl exchange chemistry coupled to mass spectrometry as a robustly S-acylated proteins in primary human T cells Morrison et al., 2015
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The human isoform ORAI1 was identified as a robustly S-acylated protein in human platelets.
source: First, the human isoform ORAI1 was identified by acyl-biotinyl exchange chemistry coupled to mass spectrometry as a robustly S-acylated proteins in primary human T cells Morrison et al., 2015 and human platelets Dowal et al., 2011.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The mouse Orai1 orthologue is reportedly S-acylated in neural stem cells.
source: Second, the mouse Orai1 orthologue is reportedly S-acylated in neural stem cells and in a T-cell hybridoma Martin et al., 2011; Li et al., 2012 according to the protein S-acylation database SwissPalm (https://swisspalm.org).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research and a database.

claim: The mouse Orai1 orthologue is reportedly S-acylated in a T-cell hybridoma.
source: Second, the mouse Orai1 orthologue is reportedly S-acylated in neural stem cells and in a T-cell hybridoma Martin et al., 2011; Li et al., 2012 according to the protein S-acylation database SwissPalm (https://swisspalm.org).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research and a database.

claim: Orai isoforms have two conserved Cys residues at potential S-acylation sites: Cys143, located in a privileged S-acylation position at the edge of the second transmembrane domain (TM2), and Cys126 within TM2.
source: Orai isoforms have two conserved Cys residues at potential S-acylation sites: Cys143, located in a privileged S-acylation position at the edge of the second transmembrane domain (TM2), and Cys126 within TM2.
evidence: This is a structural observation about ORAI1.

claim: A third Cys residue, Cys195, is sensitive to oxidation.
source: A third Cys residue, Cys195, sensitive to oxidation Bogeski et al., 2010; Alansary et al., 2016, is exposed to the extracellular side and thus unlikely to be S-acylated.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cys195 is exposed to the extracellular side and thus unlikely to be S-acylated.
source: A third Cys residue, Cys195, sensitive to oxidation Bogeski et al., 2010; Alansary et al., 2016, is exposed to the extracellular side and thus unlikely to be S-acylated.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of Cys195.

claim: Among the three Cys residues, Cys143 is the only one conserved in C. elegans.
source: Among these three Cys residue, Cys143 is the only one conserved in C. elegans (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by a figure showing sequence alignment.

claim: Cys143 but not Cys126 substitutions prevent ORAI1 S-acylation mediated by PAT3, 7 and 20.
source: Cys143 but not Cys126 substitutions prevent ORAI1 S-acylation mediated by PAT3, 7 and 20
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: PAT20 is the only regulator of ORAI1 channel function among PAT3, 7, and 20.
source: Cys143 but not Cys126 substitutions prevent ORAI1 S-acylation mediated by PAT3, 7 and 20, with PAT20 being the only regulator of channel function.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A resides in cholesterol-poor membrane domains.
source: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A resides in cholesterol-poor membrane domains
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A accumulates to a lesser extent in STIM1 puncta upon store depletion.
source: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A resides in cholesterol-poor membrane domains, accumulates to a lesser extent in STIM1 puncta upon store depletion
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A mediates reduced SOCE and ICRAC.
source: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A resides in cholesterol-poor membrane domains, accumulates to a lesser extent in STIM1 puncta upon store depletion, mediates reduced SOCE and ICRAC
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A is recruited less efficiently to the immune synapse in Jurkat T cells, severely impairing synapse formation and T cell activation.
source: S-acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A resides in cholesterol-poor membrane domains, accumulates to a lesser extent in STIM1 puncta upon store depletion, mediates reduced SOCE and ICRAC, and is recruited less efficiently to the immune synapse in Jurkat T cells, severely impairing synapse formation and T cell activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: S-acylation of ORAI1 by PAT20 controls the recruitment and function of channels and receptors at the immune synapse to mediate efficient T cell responses.
source: S-acylation of ORAI1 by PAT20 therefore controls the recruitment and function of channels and receptors at the immune synapse to mediate efficient T cell responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Endogenous ORAI1 channels incorporate palmitic acid.
source: These data show that endogenous ORAI1 channels incorporate palmitic acid and can be labelled by acyl exchange of the acyl moiety with PEG-5k.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: Endogenous ORAI1 channels can be labelled by acyl exchange of the acyl moiety with PEG-5k.
source: These data show that endogenous ORAI1 channels incorporate palmitic acid and can be labelled by acyl exchange of the acyl moiety with PEG-5k.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A single band of higher molecular weight was observed in the acyl-PEG assay, indicating that a single residue of the ORAI1 channel can be S-acylated in these conditions.
source: A single band of higher molecular weight was observed in the acyl-PEG assay, indicating that a single residue of the ORAI1 channel can be S-acylated in these conditions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of a single shifted band in Figure 1A.

claim: Only a sub-population of ORAI1 undergoes S-acylation under the experimental conditions.
source: The fact that a non-shifted ORAI1 band remains indicates that only a sub-population undergoes S-acylation under our experimental conditions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of both shifted and non-shifted bands in Figure 1A.

claim: Cells expressing ORAI1-YFP bearing the C143A substitution failed to incorporate 3H-palmitate.
source: Cells expressing ORAI1-YFP bearing the C143A substitution or the double C126A/C143A mutation, but not the single C126A mutation, failed to incorporate 3H-palmitate (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cells expressing ORAI1-YFP bearing the double C126A/C143A mutation failed to incorporate 3H-palmitate.
source: Cells expressing ORAI1-YFP bearing the C143A substitution or the double C126A/C143A mutation, but not the single C126A mutation, failed to incorporate 3H-palmitate (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cells expressing ORAI1-YFP bearing the single C126A mutation did not fail to incorporate 3H-palmitate.
source: Cells expressing ORAI1-YFP bearing the C143A substitution or the double C126A/C143A mutation, but not the single C126A mutation, failed to incorporate 3H-palmitate (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: ORAI1 channels can undergo palmitoylation at residue C143.
source: Identical results were obtained with these ORAI1-YFP mutants expressed in RPE1 cells (Figure 1D), establishing that ORAI1 channels can undergo palmitoylation at residue C143.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: C143 substitutions by alanine or serine reduced ORAI1-mediated SOCE.
source: C143 substitutions by alanine or serine, but not C126 substitutions, reduced ORAI1-mediated SOCE (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1F.

claim: C126 substitutions did not reduce ORAI1-mediated SOCE.
source: C143 substitutions by alanine or serine, but not C126 substitutions, reduced ORAI1-mediated SOCE (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1F.

claim: SOCE responses were strongly reduced in cells bearing the C143A mutation.
source: Although these cell lines were sorted for the same fluorescence and presented comparable STIM1 and ORAI1 levels as judged by epifluorescence microscopy, SOCE responses were strongly reduced in cells bearing the C143A mutation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2A–B.

claim: ICRAC current density was reduced fivefold in cells expressing the C143A mutant.
source: We then recorded ICRAC currents in HEK-S1/O1-WT and -C143A cell lines and observed a current density reduction of fivefold in cells expressing the C143A mutant in cells perfused with 10 mM BAPTA (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C–E.

claim: The currents in C143A cells retained the inward rectification, positive reversal potential, and Gd3+-sensitivity characteristic of highly Ca2+ selective CRAC currents.
source: The currents retained the inward rectification, positive reversal potential, and Gd3+-sensitivity characteristic of highly Ca2+ selective CRAC currents but activated more slowly in C143A cells (Figure 2D–F , and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2D–F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The currents in C143A cells activated more slowly.
source: The currents retained the inward rectification, positive reversal potential, and Gd3+-sensitivity characteristic of highly Ca2+ selective CRAC currents but activated more slowly in C143A cells (Figure 2D–F , and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2D–F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: C143A cells had reduced overall apparent FCDI, with a more rapid current inactivation followed by a delayed time-dependent potentiation that clipped off an initially normal FCDI.
source: C143A cells had reduced overall apparent FCDI, with a more rapid current inactivation followed by a delayed time-dependent potentiation that clipped off an initially normal FCDI (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Replacing the S-acylated Cys 143 residue within ORAI1 reduces the CRAC channel function and alters its electrophysiological properties.
source: Our Ca2+ imaging and electrophysiological data thus establish that replacing the S-acylated Cys 143 residue within ORAI1 reduces the CRAC channel function and alters its electrophysiological properties.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The HA immunoreactivity was comparable in non-permeabilised cells transiently expressing WT and C143A HA-tagged ORAI1, indicating similar surface expression.
source: The HA immunoreactivity was comparable in non-permeabilised cells transiently expressing WT and C143A HA-tagged ORAI1, indicating similar surface expression (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The ratio of TIRF vs. total YFP fluorescence was comparable in HEK-S1/O1-WT and -C143A cells, confirming that the PM fraction of ORAI is not altered by the cysteine mutation.
source: Furthermore, the ratio of TIRF vs. total YFP fluorescence was comparable in HEK-S1/O1-WT and -C143A cells, confirming that the PM fraction of ORAI is not altered by the cysteine mutation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The C143A mutation reduced the number of ORAI1 clusters.
source: The C143A mutation reduced the number of ORAI1 clusters and the average ORAI1-YFP fluorescence accumulating in STIM1-containing puncta as well as the co-localisation between mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP while the kinetics parameters of mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP cluster formation were not altered by the mutation (Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The C143A mutation reduced the average ORAI1-YFP fluorescence accumulating in STIM1-containing puncta.
source: The C143A mutation reduced the number of ORAI1 clusters and the average ORAI1-YFP fluorescence accumulating in STIM1-containing puncta as well as the co-localisation between mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP while the kinetics parameters of mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP cluster formation were not altered by the mutation (Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The C143A mutation reduced the co-localisation between mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP.
source: The C143A mutation reduced the number of ORAI1 clusters and the average ORAI1-YFP fluorescence accumulating in STIM1-containing puncta as well as the co-localisation between mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP while the kinetics parameters of mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP cluster formation were not altered by the mutation (Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The kinetics parameters of mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP cluster formation were not altered by the C143A mutation.
source: The C143A mutation reduced the number of ORAI1 clusters and the average ORAI1-YFP fluorescence accumulating in STIM1-containing puncta as well as the co-localisation between mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP while the kinetics parameters of mCh-STIM1 and ORAI1-YFP cluster formation were not altered by the mutation (Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The C143A mutant had a significantly lower diffusion coefficient indicative of a reduced mobility in membrane lipids.
source: The C143A mutant had a significantly lower diffusion coefficient indicative of a reduced mobility in membrane lipids (Figure 3—figure supplement 3 S3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A has a reduced mobility in the PM and is poorly recruited to ER-PM junctions upon store depletion.
source: These results indicate that the acylation-deficient ORAI1-C143A has a reduced mobility in the PM and is poorly recruited to ER-PM junctions upon store depletion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 3.

claim: An enhanced palmitate incorporation was observed in RPE1 and Hela cells expressing PAT3, PAT7 and PAT20.
source: An enhanced palmitate incorporation was observed in RPE1 and Hela cells expressing PAT3, PAT7 and PAT20 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Two bands migrating at ~50–65 kDa were labelled in cells overexpressing PAT3, 7 and 20, corresponding to the two ORAI1 forms generated by alternative translation initiation, fused to YFP.
source: Two bands migrating at ~50–65 kDa were labelled in cells overexpressing PAT3, 7 and 20, corresponding to the two ORAI1 forms generated by alternative translation initiation, fused to YFP.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Enforced expression of PAT20 but not of PAT3 or PAT7 in HeLa cells enhanced SOCE.
source: Enforced expression of PAT20 but not of PAT3 or PAT7 in HeLa cells enhanced SOCE (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Only siRNAs directed against PAT20 were specific in reducing SOCE in WT but not in C143A HEK S1/O1 cells.
source: All siRNAs decreased SOCE equally in WT but not in C143A HEK S1/O1 cells but only siRNAs directed against PAT20 were specific (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: PAT20 silencing mimicked the effect of the C143A mutation when an identical Ca2+ concentration was reapplied, linking the SOCE defect to the lack of ORAI1 S-acylation.
source: Importantly, PAT20 silencing mimicked the effect of the C143A mutation when an identical Ca2+ concentration was reapplied, linking the SOCE defect to the lack of ORAI1 S-acylation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: PAT20 potentiated SOCE in HEK-293 cells stably expressing ORAI1-WT but not the C143A mutant.
source: Accordingly, PAT20 potentiated SOCE in HEK-293 cells stably expressing ORAI1-WT but not the C143A mutant (Figure 4C), indicating that the gain of function conferred by increased PAT20-driven S-acylation requires this cysteine residue.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The gain of function conferred by increased PAT20-driven S-acylation requires the Cys143 residue.
source: Accordingly, PAT20 potentiated SOCE in HEK-293 cells stably expressing ORAI1-WT but not the C143A mutant (Figure 4C), indicating that the gain of function conferred by increased PAT20-driven S-acylation requires this cysteine residue.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: PAT20 overexpression increased the fraction of WT ORAI1-YFP located in lipid rafts, without altering the distribution of the C143A channel.
source: PAT20 overexpression increased the fraction of WT ORAI1-YFP located in lipid rafts, without altering the distribution of the C143A channel (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: PAT3, 7 and 20 S-acylate ORAI1 on a single residue, Cys143.
source: These experiments indicate that PAT3, 7 and 20 S-acylate ORAI1 on a single residue, Cys143, and that PAT20 levels limit channel function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: PAT20 levels limit ORAI1 channel function.
source: These experiments indicate that PAT3, 7 and 20 S-acylate ORAI1 on a single residue, Cys143, and that PAT20 levels limit channel function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: PAT20-mediated S-acylation of Cys143 modifies the lipid preference of the ORAI1 channel to promote its accumulation in lipid rafts.
source: PAT20-mediated S-acylation of Cys143 modifies the lipid preference of the ORAI1 channel to promote its accumulation in lipid rafts.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 4D.

claim: SOCE was severely blunted in ORAI1-deficient Jurkat T cells.
source: To assess whether ORAI1 S-acylation impacts T cell function, we generated by CRISPR an ORAI1-deficient Jurkat T cell line, in which SOCE was severely blunted (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Stable transduction of ORAI1-WT restored SOCE in ORAI1-deficient Jurkat T cells.
source: Stable transduction of ORAI1-WT restored SOCE in these cells while ORAI1-C143A, expressed at comparable levels at the PM, was ineffective (Figure 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: ORAI1-C143A, expressed at comparable levels at the PM, was ineffective in restoring SOCE in ORAI1-deficient Jurkat T cells.
source: Stable transduction of ORAI1-WT restored SOCE in these cells while ORAI1-C143A, expressed at comparable levels at the PM, was ineffective (Figure 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Activation of the TCR with CD3/CD28 beads evoked long-lasting Ca2+ elevations in CRISPR ORAI1+ ORAI1 WT stable cells.
source: Activation of the TCR with CD3/CD28 beads evoked long-lasting Ca2+ elevations in CRISPR ORAI1+ ORAI1 WT stable cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Cells reconstituted with ORAI1-C143A exhibited smaller and more transient Ca2+ responses to TCR activation.
source: In contrast, cells reconstituted with ORAI1-C143A exhibited smaller and more transient responses (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Among all 23 PAT isoforms overexpression of only PAT 3, 7, and 20 increased palmitate incorporation in ORAI1-deficient Jurkat T cells reconstituted with ORAI1-WT but not with the C143A mutant.
source: Among all 23 PAT isoforms overexpression of only PAT 3, 7, and 20 increased palmitate incorporation in ORAI1-deficient Jurkat T cells reconstituted with ORAI1-WT but not with the C143A mutant, confirming that ORAI1 is S-acylated by these enzymes in immune cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: PAT20 expression augmented SOCE in WT Jurkat cells but had no effect in cells lacking ORAI1.
source: Accordingly, PAT20 expression augmented SOCE in WT cells but had no effect in cells lacking ORAI1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: ORAI1 ablation aborted NFAT-dependent transcription in Jurkat T cells treated with Tg.
source: ORAI1 ablation aborted NFAT-dependent transcription and reduced nuclear translocation of endogenous NFATC1 in cells treated with Tg (Figure 5D–E)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5D–E.

claim: ORAI1 ablation reduced nuclear translocation of endogenous NFATC1 in Jurkat T cells treated with Tg.
source: ORAI1 ablation aborted NFAT-dependent transcription and reduced nuclear translocation of endogenous NFATC1 in cells treated with Tg (Figure 5D–E)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5D–E.

claim: ORAI1 ablation prevented the potentiating effects of PAT20 expression on IL-2 production evoked by Tg and CD3-coated plates.
source: ORAI1 ablation aborted NFAT-dependent transcription and reduced nuclear translocation of endogenous NFATC1 in cells treated with Tg (Figure 5D–E) and prevented the potentiating effects of PAT20 expression on IL-2 production evoked by Tg and CD3-coated plates (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: Re-expression of WT ORAI1 potentiated NFAT-dependent transcription in ORAI1-deficient Jurkat cells treated with Tg compared to C143A.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5D–E and Figure 5—figure supplement 6.

claim: Re-expression of WT ORAI1 potentiated NFATC1 nuclear translocation in ORAI1-deficient Jurkat cells treated with Tg compared to C143A.

claim: CD3-coated plates increased NFATC1 translocation in Jurkat cells reconstituted with WT but not with C143A ORAI1.

claim: No NFAT luciferase response was observed in Jurkat T cells reconstituted with ORAI1-C143A after 24 hr of co-culture with SEE-pulsed Raji cells.

claim: C143A ORAI1-YFP was enriched in the opposite pole, forming distal caps, in nearly 60 % of cells.

claim: C143A ORAI1-YFP remained evenly distributed between the IS and distal caps.

evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The acylation site of ORAI1 is Cys143 on the cytosolic rim of the second TM domain.

claim: Orai1 is rapidly S-acylated at cysteine 143 upon ER Ca2+ store depletion.
